Maintenance Report — MNT-0068-009

Asset: WELL-0068 (SW-24 Well 068, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 28 Sep 2024 08:00 · Finished: 15 Oct 2024 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 419 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0068-0069 on 2024-09-26 Report written: 16 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0068-0069 showed the wellhead at 30.2 °C with the air at 24.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Total17,850

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0068-015

Asset: WELL-0068 (SW-24 Well 068, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 04 Oct 2025 08:00 · Finished: 21 Oct 2025 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 413 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0068-0120 on 2025-10-02 Report written: 22 Oct 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0068-0120 showed the wellhead at 24.4 °C with the air at 24.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0068-021

Asset: WELL-0068 (SW-24 Well 068, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 Oct 2026 08:00 · Finished: 06 Oct 2026 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 72 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0068-0172 on 2026-10-01 Report written: 07 Oct 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0068-0172 showed the wellhead at 26.1 °C with the air at 24.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
